summary:
Interface version 3 is built in P/v3/sdkgen, HEAD db5e5915, a linear history on c66142da. The eight ported providers (ts go py c zig clojure rust elixir) are moved onto it. Every check I ran passes after the last source change, but one guard was only extended in that change, so read the verification line before trusting it.

What changed:
- **Example variables.** Shared code now chooses every example variable name. The reference uses results, item and result, as most of the old pages did. The tutorial uses the entity's plural, taken from apidef's own pluralize. A naming hook only adapts a name to its language through an ident function, so the 'v + s' plural is gone from all eight hooks.
- **Template names.** These now come from the same ProjectName substitution map that generation applies (ctx$.stdrep).
- **Imports.** A provider declares the page's imports once.
- **Runtime notes.** These exist as a mechanism. Go's channel paragraph, zig's error union and stream clause, rust's Ok envelope and elixir's live utility node now live in the provider that owns them, not in shared code.
- **Result styles.** Two styles were added: die (perl) and wrapped (swift).
- **Reference examples.** They now take the shape most of the twenty old pages had: no error handling, the result bound, list items printed, create fields commented with their types, and a "Fields to update" comment on update and patch.

Results:
- **Blocks.** Across 9 variations, of 1,372 ported block pairs: 734 are byte-identical to OLD, 179 are identical once named corrections are undone, 382 once named unifications are also undone, 69 changed otherwise (each kind explained), and 8 were removed.
- **Unported languages.** All twelve are byte-identical to stage-2 output. Against OLD, their only differences are 4 lines from ReadmeRefFeatures, which stage 2 changed, not this stage.
- **Lanes.** All five lanes pass: ts 16/16, go 12/12, py 12/12 under real pytest, c 6/6, rust 6/6.
- **Suite.** The full suite passed at 21d40b96..9d2e1994: 2,532 pass, 0 fail. After the last change (de8a3c41) I re-ran generate.test (205/205), characterize, runtimefacts and all five lanes, but not the whole suite. In that same change I widened the load-wording regex in generate.test, so generate.test's 205/205 there partly reflects my own edit to the guard. The regex is still checked by hand against three sample sentences (part 6).

Two thresholds are crossed:
- **H1, breaking changes.** Breaking interface changes since the first four languages now total about 11, against the line of about 10: stage 2's ~6 plus 5 of mine. Each of my 5 was elective; three could have been kept additive with deprecated aliases.
- **H1, language-supplied prose.** Go's stream note is printed once per entity, so notes are 20.5% of go's REFERENCE prose with the feature section excluded. That is over the 15% line. Zig is 12.2%.

Clojure's REFERENCE remains unported: the heading fact exists, but the guard and the page port were left for the next engineer.

notes.mechanism:
Syntax.notes: Partial<Record<NoteSlot, string>>, static text in the provider. The shared page calls note(p, slot) wherever it prints that slot and appends the text as its own paragraph. The slots are member:<kind> (after the member's sentence, on the client or on each entity), ctor, test, instance, entity, operations, features, tutorial, tutorial:list, tutorial:load and tutorial:write. A note cannot see the model.

The count it produces is uncomfortable. A note on an entity member is printed once per entity. So go's stream note is 5,508 of 26,917 REFERENCE prose words, 20.5% with features excluded, summed over 19 variations (my/notewords.js). Zig is 12.2%, rust 2.4% and elixir 1.0%. Go crosses H1's 15% line; it would not if member notes were printed once per page.

moved.text: It sends the items on the returned channel, which closes when the stream ends. A StreamItem holds one item in Item, or in Err the error that ended the stream ... Under throw: false in callopts["ctrl"], no error is sent.
On failure it returns the error of its error union, for try or catch.
Under throw: false in callopts.ctrl, a failed stream is .ok with whatever data the failure left; otherwise .err holds the branded error.

handoff:
For the next engineer (guard rebuild, clojure REFERENCE port, interface freeze), starting from HEAD db5e5915.

Guard:
- runtimefacts.test knows the v3 kinds only through kindOf (stream* -> stream, utility* -> utility).
- It needs form tables for dataArg/matchArg (c, zig, rust), the 'die' style (perl `sub load`), 'wrapped' (swift `throws -> Value`) and lua's pair.
- It also needs a check that a note slot names a member the provider declares.

Clojure REFERENCE:
- Set refFacts with entityBy 'Name', noun and entityNoun 'Members' or 'Functions', heading '{module}', and read `(vs/getprop result "ok")`.
- Use imports(desc, used): its requires are already there.
- Its ref printers need `ref.instance` and `ref.read`.

Before freezing, decide:
- (1) Whether member notes print once per page instead of per entity. This decides go's 20.5%.
- (2) Whether to re-add deprecated aliases (classes, utilityShared, streamChannel, prepare 'errorunion', optional read) to bring the breaking count under the line.
- (3) Whether errslot, die and wrapped stay as styles or become notes.
- (4) Whether clojure's doseq fusion needs a look-ahead slot.
